submission.name: Garden Signs
submission.tagline: Show a garden sign, get a clearer way to share what you need.
submission.inspiration: Volunteers at a community garden may not share a first language, and simple signs or instructions can be hard to communicate quickly. We wanted to combine a local garden resource map with a camera tool that recognizes a few hand-spelled letters, so people can find useful places and share short labels.
submission.what_it_does: The map prototype collects nearby gardens, public growing spaces, and selected community resources from open listings. A separate webcam experiment tries to recognize ASL fingerspelling and display the detected letters as text. We pictured using that to search or label a map marker, but the two parts are not connected yet and the gesture model is limited to individual letters.
submission.how_we_built_it: The map interface uses React, Vite, Tailwind, and Leaflet, with a small FastAPI service and SQLite for saved markers. OpenStreetMap data and a few public resource sources provide starting locations, while Gemini can draft short descriptions from available listing details. For the second interaction, we built a browser camera experiment that classifies hand shapes and groups recognized letters into text. The map and camera tools run as separate prototypes; connecting recognized words to map search is the next integration step.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Listings from different sources use inconsistent categories and can be out of date, so a combined map can still mislead. Webcam recognition also depends on framing and lighting, and letter-by-letter output is slow for real conversation. We did not have time to link the camera results to the map or test the flow with garden volunteers.
submission.accomplishments: We are proud to have two concrete pieces: a map with several kinds of community locations and a small fingerspelling recognition demo. Working on both showed us how a communication aid could fit into a practical local-resource tool.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned the tradeoffs involved in combining open map data with manually saved locations, and how much visual input conditions affect a webcam classifier. Gemini helped draft concise listing descriptions, while our camera experiment taught us that recognition needs a clear task and good framing. We also learned that separate prototypes need a shared data shape before they can feel like one app.
submission.whats_next: We would connect recognized letters to a simple place search or marker label, then improve recognition for short words. We would also add a way for garden groups to correct listings and flag outdated information.
